messages:
oncall-bot: Paging oncall: multiple serving nodes in cluster 'eu-west-2a' reporting repeated CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Initial signal: healthcheck flapping + high kernel drops on IB. Pager: P12345.

oncall-bot: Symptoms: 30% 5xx increase for /v1/generate, 2 model-serving pods per node crashing with SIGSEGV/CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN.

lisa: acknowleged, I'm on it. Pulling logs and checking fabric telemetry.

mike: seeing a ton of MLX5 link errors on nodes eqw-ru-02/03. `dmesg` shows: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_ib: HCA 0000:81:00.0: link down
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mdev: PF link flap, timeout
```

mike: also RDMA counters: tx_dropped rising, qp timeouts occasionally.

anya: is this correlated with a config rollout? I can see a canary bump of model x-large yesterday but traffic pattern hasn't changed much.

lisa: not a rollout. CPU and memory on node look normal prior to crashes. Kernel logs + IB counters indicate brief blackhole periods where packets never get acked -> long tail latencies -> serving runtime stalls -> KV cache grows -> CUDA OOM when requests reflow.

infra-bot: Automated mitigation suggestion: 1) move affected pods to tcp-only nodes (disable RDMA) 2) enable model-fallback to quantized variant 3) cordon problematic hosts.

mike: I'm going to cordon eqw-ru-02 now and drain pods to other racks. Running: `kubectl cordon eqw-ru-02 && kubectl drain eqw-ru-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --pod-selector=app=redwood-runtime`

lisa: i'll flip routing to prefer eu-west-2b for new requests. Can someone trigger the revert to TCP for the serving daemon on the drained nodes?

anya: on it. Patching daemonset to set `RDMA_ENABLED=false` on node selector for fallback pool. Patch applied to pool-fallback-*-ds.

mike: restart sequence started. Observed one pod come up on eu-west-2b and begin serving. Latency immediately improved for that pod.

customer_support: ticket queue: a few customer conversations reporting elevated 5xx for the past 10 minutes; estimated impacted customers ~7 (mid-late tier). We're sending template status update.

lisa: quick note for postmortem: the failure mode is intermittent IB blackholing causing request bursts to pile into runtime KV cache and then blow GPU memory on resume. Need improved backpressure.

mike: confirmed: after cordon+drain+tcp-fallback, no further CUDA OOMs on surviving nodes. 5xx rate dropping back down.

infra-bot: Action items created: AKT-332 (fabric probe/alert tuning), AKT-333 (runtime backpressure patch), AKT-334 (automatic model variant fallback on packetloss).

anya: handoff: lisa, I'm going to sleep on this, you take the pager for the next 2 hours; i'll stay available for escalation.

lisa: taking handoff. I'll keep fabric traces open and collect pcap from eqw-ru-02/03 for the network team: `tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/eqw-ru-02-03-prefrag.pcap`

sre_pager: reminder: open status page if customer impact persists > 30m.

mike: immediate followups I'll do: i) collect heap/KV cache snapshot from crashed containers ii) add a short-circuit in runtime to evict device cache when qp timeouts exceed threshold iii) schedule a maintenance window to repro in lab with stress tool.

lisa: posting interim summary to #incidents and #customer-updates in 5. Current state: fabric instability detected -> cordon+drain+tcp-fallback applied -> 5xxs decreasing -> monitoring.

customer_support: thanks, we pushed customer note: "We're aware of elevated errors in eu-west-2 and are actively mitigating; further updates in ~30m."

oncall-bot: note: escalation threshold cleared. If errors reappear, the bot will repage.

mike: log snippets attached to incident P12345: `runtime: eviction triggered due to device memory pressure, freeing 2.3GB` and `ib_warn: packet_retransmit 4x spike`.

lisa: last check: 5xxs at baseline, GPU memory OK, no new IB link down events for 4m. Marking mitigation stable, will draft postmortem that includes timeline and recommended mitigations.

anya: thanks team. Follow-ups assigned.

sre_pager: handoff complete.
